newsitem.title: UK: Sterling skids versus mark and dollar in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Sterling skids versus mark and dollar in Europe.

text.p: Sterling skid one pfennig and over half a cent to below 3.05 and $1.65 as dollar/mark stormed to 7-1/2 year peaks against the mark and a survey highlighted concern over export orders, choked off by a booming pound.
"Clearly, the banks are not quite as sure about sterling," said a trader at Bank of Boston. Traders noted persistent sterling/mark selling from a UK clearing bank.
Cable was also shaky amid broad dollar strength. The dollar also pushed to two-month highs against the yen and to its highest since August 1993 against the Swiss franc.

Although the pound is looking toppy on the charts - it reached a peak high of 3.0878 marks last week, its highest since August 1989 - it is unlikely to come under hefty selling pressure in the short-term, traders said.
"The pound has been overbought for some time, but it should remain propped short-term," said a trader at a UK bank.

At 1145 GMT, sterling/mark was trading at 3.0485/95 against 3.0560/70 in late Europe and session peaks of 3.0627. Cable was at $1.6511/21 against $1.6616/26, and down from $1.6660 peaks. Cable is well supported at $1.65, traders said.
Analysts said waning confidence in European monetary union's (EMU) timetable and perceptions of even higher rates in the UK will also help.
